newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's CSI to strike again; Inespal works on.
newsitem.headline: Spain's CSI to strike again; Inespal works on.

text.p: Workers at Spain's state-owned steel firm Corporacion Siderugica Integral (CSI) will hold a final strike before summer vacations on Thursday to protest sale plans for the firm, a spokesman for UGT union told Reuters.
Separately, state-owned aluminium producer Inespal called off a strike for the second-week running, the spokesman said.
CSI has held short strikes every week for the past few weeks in anger at Spain's plans to sell a 35-percent stake in the group.

The government has received two competing offers for the stake -- from Usinor and from Arbed -- but has yet to announce a decision, which is expected to be taken on August 1 or right after the August summer holiday.

After the sale of this 35 percent stake, Spain is expected to sell another stake of between 10 and 25 percent of CSI to non-technological domestic or international partners. The third step is a public share offering for the remaining tranche, between 55 and 40 percent, probably in the autumn.
The UGT spokesman said that at Inespal, union representatives were expected to meet with the government next week over its talks with Aluminum Co of America (Alcoa).
SEPI, the state holding group which controls Inespal, signed a preliminary agreement for Alcoa to buy Inespal's main businesses by the end of 1997 in February.
